title: Migration 72 — the person who uploads a document may not be the person who clears it
description: Applies the farmer document substrate, 64 and 65 (the review attribution and clarification path 72's constraint depends on, since it compares against reviewed_by which fn_farmer_documents_set_reviewer assigns), 67 (the ledger 72 refuses to run without) and 68 (the decision gate, whose BEFORE UPDATE ordering is what makes the constraint see the DECIDING session rather than whatever the caller sent), then 72. The public Governance page claimed this separation was 'enforced in the database' while farmer_documents had no uploaded_by column at all — the comparison could not be made, so the claim was never published and this migration is what would make it true. VERIFY covers the catalog: the column on both tables typed as reviewed_by is, the BEFORE INSERT trigger and that its function assigns outright rather than coalescing the caller's value (a coalesce would look correct and let any caller name its own uploader), the constraint present and VALID rather than merely added NOT VALID, the self-recorded ledger row, and section E which asserts the deliberate NULL branch — the hole that scopes the public claim to documents uploaded AFTER the apply, since nothing attributes historical rows. Rollback removes the constraint, trigger and function, and drops both columns ONLY because nothing was ever stamped here: with real attributions in them it refuses and demands an explicit opt-in, because nothing else in the database records who uploaded a document and dropping the column discards that permanently. Protecting zero attributions is not a safety property, it is residue — the same lesson the rollback-symmetry check taught migration 69.

verify.note: A the column on farmer_documents AND on the deletion record, typed against reviewed_by rather than a literal so a type drift between the two values the constraint compares is what fails. B the BEFORE INSERT ROW trigger and, more importantly, that its function assigns NEW.uploaded_by := auth.uid() OUTRIGHT — a coalesce of the caller's value would pass a structural check and defeat the entire control, so the body is read. C the constraint exists AND is convalidated: NOT VALID would mean it governs new rows only and was never checked against what is already there, which is a weaker claim wearing the same name. It also asserts the pending exemption, without which no document could ever be inserted. D the ledger row is self-recorded, not backfilled — the state migration 66 sits in is indistinguishable from never having been applied. E asserts the NULL branch rather than merely mentioning it: if someone later makes the column NOT NULL or drops the exemption, the scope of the public claim has changed and E is where that surfaces.
